# bea

Ghent, Belgium. 34. Intensive-care nurse on a rotating roster: a block of
three or four twelve-hour nights, days off, then a stretch of day shifts. The
record runs from 2029-09-03 to 2030-06-30.

She swims and lifts. Neither is a project; both are things she fits around
whichever half of the clock she is currently living in.

## What she is for

Every other persona in this corpus sleeps at night. That means an engine that
anchors a day to the calendar and an engine that anchors it to the athlete's
sleep agree on all ten of them, and the corpus cannot tell the two apart.
bea is the record where they disagree.

After a night shift she sleeps roughly 09:00 to 16:00. Her first meal is at
17:00. Her session, when there is one, is at 18:30. The part of her day that
behaves like a morning happens in the evening.

## What she does not have

No injury, no illness, no dramatic arc. Her record is unremarkable in every
respect except when things happen, which is the point: a persona carrying a
confound and a story at once cannot say which one an engine tripped over.

## The roster

Deterministic and its own random stream, so the shift pattern can be changed
without moving a single step count behind it. Three block shapes, chosen per
block:

- 3 nights, 3 off, 4 days, 2 off
- 4 nights, 4 off, 3 days, 2 off
- 3 nights, 4 off, 5 days, 2 off

Everything else in her record is downstream of that label - including the
regimes rows, whose intervals are read off the roster rather than written
beside it, so the narrative and the numbers cannot drift apart.
